 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Oct 29, 2026, 18:50:00 IST SUMMARY Karwa Chauth 2026 is being observed on Thursday, October 29, with married Hindu women across India celebrating the auspicious festival with great devotion, love and enthusiasm. The festival holds special significance in North India, particularly in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi, where women observe a day-long fast for the long life, good health, happiness and prosperity of their husbands. Over the years, the festival has also evolved into a celebration of love, companionship and togetherness among married couples. 
 On this special occasion, women traditionally observe a nirjala vrat, refraining from food and water from sunrise until moonrise. The day begins early with the customary Sargi meal, which is usually prepared or gifted by the mother-in-law. The pre-dawn meal helps women prepare for the day-long fast. After sunrise, devotees abstain from eating and drinking while following the traditional customs and rituals associated with the festival. 
 As the day progresses, women prepare for the evening celebrations by dressing in traditional attire, often choosing red, maroon or other festive colours. They adorn themselves with jewellery, apply mehendi and decorate their puja thalis with essentials required for the rituals. In many households, women gather with friends and family members to perform the traditional Karwa Chauth puja and listen to the Karwa Chauth Katha, which recounts the religious significance of the fast and highlights the themes of devotion, faith and marital commitment. 
 One of the most awaited moments of Karwa Chauth is the moonrise, which marks the conclusion of the day-long fast. After sighting the Moon, women offer Arghya and perform the customary rituals. Traditionally, they look at the Moon through a sieve and then look at their husbands before breaking their fast. Husbands often offer their wives water and the first morsel of food, symbolising affection, care and mutual commitment. 
 The exact moonrise time varies from city to city, making it important for devotees to check their local timings before performing the evening rituals. The puja muhurat and moonrise timings are among the most searched details during the festival. 
 Karwa Chauth is more than a religious observance; it is a cherished cultural tradition that celebrates the emotional bond between married couples and brings families together. While customs may differ across regions and households, the spirit of love, faith and togetherness remains central to the celebration. 
 Stay tuned to our Karwa Chauth 2026 LIVE blog for the latest updates on city-wise moonrise timings, puja muhurat, traditional rituals, celebrity celebrations and festive developments from across the country. Live Events 
 18:50 (IST) Oct 29 Karwa Chauth 2026: History and significance of the festival of love Karwa Chauth is not only a ceremony of fasting, but it also has significant cultural and historical importance. It is said that the festival imitates the worship of Goddess Parvati, who fasted in order to win the love of Lord Shiva as a husband. Married women also carry out this fast with the greatest degree of devotion so that they can have a long life and a healthy existence for their husbands. It is also believed that the day brings good fortune, prosperity, and harmony to the family. 
Besides praying to their husbands, women also worship Lord Shiva, Goddess Parvati, Lord Ganesha, and Karwa Mata to bless them in the life of a happy and successful marriage. The fast is also a sign of faith and tradition, keeping the family ties together, not just love and commitment.

During Karwa Chauth, women look at the moon and their husbands through a sieve (called a chalni) to symbolize spiritual filtering, reverence, and devotion. 
The mesh of the sieve is believed to filter out negative energy, distractions, or harsh influences, allowing only pure, calm light and love to pass through to the husband. The sieve acts as a traditional, light veil through which a wife shyly or reverently catches a glimpse of her husband's face, echoing traditional customs of modesty.

 16:15 (IST) Oct 29 Karwa Chauth 2026 Live Update: Puja Vidhi for Performing Karwa Chauth Alone If you’re celebrating Karwa Chauth alone this year, there’s no need to worry about performing the puja. Women can use a picture or a small idol of Goddess Gauri/Parvati to perform the Karwa Chauth puja. Simply place the image or clay idol at your puja space and follow the ritual as usual. 
 16:05 (IST) Oct 29 Karwa Chauth 2026: Why Do Married Women Wait for the Moon to Rise Before Breaking Their Fast? The name itself tells part of the story. “Karwa” is an earthen pot with a spout. “Chauth” means fourth. The festival falls on the fourth lunar day after the full moon in the month of Kartik. In Vedic astrology, the Moon, or Chandra, governs the mind and emotions. It’s also connected with nourishment and longevity. Old texts link it with Soma, the divine nectar of the gods, believed to sustain life. So offering prayers to the Moon for a husband’s long life makes clear sense. The Moon represents emotional bonds and life-giving energy. A woman fasting all day and then greeting the Moon is, symbolically, asking that same energy to protect her marriage. 
 The Moon’s cycle adds meaning too. It waxes and wanes, disappears and returns, month after month. Many see that steady return as a reflection of the hope that a marriage, too, will keep renewing itself through difficult phases.

But spotting two green parrots together has a different significance. The parrot, known as Shuka, is associated with Kamadeva, the deity of love and attraction. A pair of green parrots is therefore regarded in some folk interpretations as a favourable symbol of affection, attraction and companionship. On Karwa Chauth, when prayers are offered for marital wellbeing, such a sighting is considered particularly meaningful. Many people mistake it for a crow, but it is the Bharadwaj Pakshi, commonly known as the Greater Coucal. In several Shakun traditions, seeing this bird is considered a favourable omen. Its appearance on Karwa Chauth is popularly associated with good news, improvements in family circumstances, and the resolution of pending matters. For couples dealing with family disagreements or prolonged uncertainty over an important decision, such a sighting is traditionally interpreted positively. The Greater Coucal is usually found around gardens, bushes and areas with dense vegetation. It is often heard before it is seen. 15:00 (IST) Oct 29 Karwa Chauth 2026: Seeing these 3 birds is considered auspcious for married life On Karwa Chauth, most women spend the day waiting for Chandra Darshan. From checking the moonrise time to preparing the puja thali, almost everything revolves around the Moon. But what about the birds you see during the day? In Indian traditions, observing birds and their behaviour has been an important part of Shakun Shastra. With Karwa Chauth on October 29 this year, there are three bird sightings worth knowing about, particularly from the perspective of marital happiness and family wellbeing. 14:45 (IST) Oct 29 Karwa Chauth 2026: 5 last-minute gift ideas for your wife that feel personal
 When was the last time you told your wife what you appreciate about her, without waiting for a special occasion? Karwa Chauth can be a good opportunity to do just that. 
 Write her a letter recalling a favourite memory, something you admire about her, or a small moment in your relationship that still makes you smile. Pair it with a framed photograph or a small personalised keepsake. 
 It costs very little, but the personal details can make it a gift she wants to hold on to.

A reservation at her favourite restaurant, a visit to a café she has been wanting to try or an evening spent enjoying her favourite dessert can make the day memorable. 
 If you cannot go out, plan a special dinner at home. Take care of the arrangements yourself so she can enjoy the evening without having to organise everything.

A delicate pendant, a pair of earrings or a simple bracelet can make a lovely gift without requiring you to buy an elaborate set. 
 Look at the accessories she already wears to understand her style. A piece that matches her everyday outfits is more likely to become a favourite than something chosen simply because it looks festive.

You do not need an elaborate surprise or an expensive present to make her smile. Sometimes, the best gifts are the ones that show you have been paying attention to the little things she likes. 
 Perhaps she has been talking about a particular perfume, saving a dessert place on Instagram, or wishing she had more time for herself. These everyday conversations can give you better gift ideas than a last-minute shopping search. Here are five thoughtful gifts you can still consider for your wife this Karwa Chauth.

Read full story › 14:15 (IST) Oct 29 Karwa Chauth 2026 live updates: 5 must-have bhog for Karwa Chauth Karwa Chauth is not only a day of fasting and devotion but also a time for offering gratitude through traditional bhog (food offerings) to Goddess Parvati, Lord Shiva, and the Moon God.
 1. Sargi Thali Delights: A pre-dawn meal, gifted by the mothers-in-law, usually includes pheni, dry fruits, fruits, and coconut.
 2. Halwa-Poori: This combo is a traditional offering in almost every North Indian household during Karwa Chauth.
 3. Mathri and Namak Pare: These snacks represent stability and endurance—qualities essential for a strong marriage.
 4. Rice Kheer: This sweet dish holds a special place in Hindu rituals, and during Karwa Chauth, it’s offered to the Moon God as part of the bhog.
 5. Fruits and Dry Fruits: Fruits and dry fruits are an indispensable part of the bhog thali.
 14:00 (IST) Oct 29 Karwa Chauth 2026: Moon not visible due to Cyclone Arnab? Here are 3 traditional ways to break the fast Worship a silver coin as a symbol of the moon:
In astrology, silver is related to Chandra Dev. If you have a silver coin or a round silver piece at home, you may use it as a symbolic representation of the Moon. Place it on a clean plate, worship it with devotion, and offer Arghya after the prescribed local moonrise time. The remaining rituals can be completed according to your household customs.
 13:45 (IST) Oct 29 Karwa Chauth 2026: Moon not visible due to Cyclone Arnab? Here are 3 traditional ways to break the fast Make a moon using rice :
 This is another simple traditional practice that can be performed at home. Place a red or yellow cloth on a clean wooden chowki. Using uncooked rice (Akshat), make the shape of the Moon on the cloth. After the local moonrise time, look at this symbolic Moon through the Karwa Chauth sieve (Chhalni), offer prayers, and chant ॐ चंद्राय नमः or ॐ सोम सोमाय नमः. You can then perform the puja and Arghya according to your family tradition.
 13:30 (IST) Oct 29 Karwa Chauth 2026: Moon not visible due to Cyclone Arnab? Here are 3 traditional ways to break the fast Seek Chandra Darshan through Lord Shiva:
 We all know Lord Shiva as Chandrashekhar, the one who holds the Moon on his head. If the Moon remains hidden behind clouds, women can seek Chandra Darshan through the crescent Moon on Lord Shiva's head. You may visit a nearby Shiva temple or use a picture or idol of Lord Shiva available at home. After the local moonrise time, worship Lord Shiva, offer prayers to Chandra Dev through the Moon depicted on his head, and offer the Arghya.

 10:30 (IST) Oct 29 What rituals are followed during Karwa Chauth? Here is the complete fasting guide:
 Before dawn: 
 Wake up early and have the sargi your mother-in-law sends. 
 It usually has dry fruits, pheni or kheer, fresh fruits, and mathri. 
 Drink plenty of water at this time, since most women don't have any during the day.
 Through the day: Take it easy, avoid heavy work and long trips, and rest in the afternoon if you can. 
 Many women put on mehendi a day earlier. On the evening of the vrat, they dress in red, maroon or other bridal colours. 
 Solah shringar is traditional, but a simple, neat outfit is just as good. 
 Getting the puja ready: Set up your thali with roli, rice, a diya, sweets, a karwa filled with water, and a chalni (sieve). 
 Place a picture of Karva Mata on the wall or on a wooden plank, or draw one. 
 At the puja time: Light the lamp and pray to Ganesha first. Then pray to Karva Mata, along with Shiva and Parvati, and listen to the katha. If you are sitting in a group, you can pass your thalis around seven times while singing traditional songs. 
 When the moon rises, look at the moon through the chalni and offer water from the karwa. Then look at your husband through the same chalni. He gives you your first sip of water and a sweet, and that concludes the fast. 
 Follow it with a light dinner, since a heavy meal on an empty stomach can upset you.

It is a nirjala fast, with no food or water from sunrise to moonrise. In the present day, husbands also join in; couples celebrate equality, and over the years, rituals and festivals like this have helped strengthen social bonds among women, including with in-laws and friends. 10:00 (IST) Oct 29 Legend behind Karwachauth: The story of Veeravati There is an age-old mythological legend behind the celebration of Karwachauth surrounding Veeravati, who was the only sister of seven brothers, and they adored her. After her marriage, she came to her parents' home for her first Karwa Chauth. She fasted without food or water, and by evening hunger and thirst made her faint. Her brothers could not bear to see her suffer. They lit a fire behind a peepal tree and held a sieve in front of it, so the glow looked like the rising moon. Veervati believed them, offered arghya to the false moon and ate. Soon after, news came that her husband had died. Heartbroken, she sat beside his body for a year, praying without pause. Goddess Parvati told her the fast had been broken before the real moonrise. She advised Veervati to keep every Chaturthi vrat that year and to observe the next Karwa Chauth with complete faith. Veervati did, and her husband's life was restored. The story is that the fast is complete only when the real moon is seen. 09:45 (IST) Oct 29 Who is worshipped on Karwachauth? Karva Mata, a form of Goddess Parvati linked with marital bliss, is worshipped with Lord Shiva, along with Ganesha and Kartikeya. Chaturthi is Ganesha's tithi, so he is the first one to be prayed to, and then the final arghya is given to the moon. Chandra rules the mind, emotions, and the bond of care between two people. Moon worship on this day is meant to bring peace into married life and protect the husband's health and long life. 09:30 (IST) Oct 29 Karwachauth 2026: Puja muhurat, fasting hours and moonrise According to Drik Panchang, the fast begins at 6:31 AM (sunrise). According to Drikpanchang, the Chaturthi tithi starts at 1:06 AM on 29 October and ends at 10:09 PM that night, so the vrat is kept on 29 October across India. The reason behind this is that Chaturthi must be observed when the moon rises, because the fast ends with Chandra puja. 09:00 (IST) Oct 29 Karwa Chauth 2026: 5 things not to do for Karwa Chauth 1.
